Prevention: Green stink bugs are insects which feed on the sap of various crop plants.
Use of early maturing crop varieties as trap crops for control actions to reduce pest populations (e.g. cowpeas, beans, crucierous plants).
Trap crops should be ploughed in to prevent adult pests from migrating to the main crop.
Removal of plant material post-harvest to reduce overwintering insect numbers.
Employ suitable crop sanitation practices such as:
Actively removing dead plant parts and weeds from plots.
Intercropping or rotating crops with non- related crops such as maize or sorghum.
Monitoring: To monitor for infestation, observe all plant parts, insect is mostly found feeding on fruiting parts and shoots.
Eggs are cream/yellow, slightly elongated and packed tightly on leaves.
As they develop they change colour to pink and then bright orange.
Nymphs are initially black, wingless and have four body segments.
Colouration changes throughout development before turning green.
Adults are large green shield bugs, roughly 15 mm long.
They can typically be identified by three white dots on the front of the shield.
Insects puncture plant tissue, leaving small, hard brown/black spots which reduces growth of immature fruit and premature defoliation.
Puncture holes in crops may cause secondary fungal or bacterial infections, check diseased plants for these holes to avoid misdiagnosis.
Use sweep nets to monitor for stink bug populations, if one stink bug is found per meter row of sweeping then consider direct control actions.
Direct Control: Remove old crops and stumps, destroy by burning or burying 50 cm below ground.
Spray with botanical extracts e.g. neem seed extract (take 50 g mix in 2
L of water, boil for 15 minutes, allow to cool and spray 3 times at 2 week intervals).
Spray plants with soapy water to remove insects.
Handpick any that are found and destroy.
Beauveria bassiana products and follow instructions on the label.
